stories.title: Where I grew up
stories.text: I grew up in Rajgangpur, a small town in Odisha, India. My interest in building things came later.

stories.title: Where I was based in October 2026
stories.text: I spent the two years before October 2026 nomading across Southeast Asia. As of October 2026, I was travelling across countries in the European Union. My location changes.

stories.title: How I introduce my work
stories.text: I build software and help good products get found. I keep several projects going because I like both sides of that problem.

stories.title: An oddly specific strength
stories.text: I'm good at finding the expensive, annoying step everyone treats as inevitable and asking whether it actually needs to exist.

stories.title: My favorite food
stories.text: I love Indian food. My favorite is malai kofta with tandoori roti. I would defend that choice in court, preferably over lunch.

stories.title: A food preference
stories.text: I don't eat red meat. I respect its right to exist, just far away from my plate.

stories.title: Books I like
stories.text: Books I like include Purple Cow by Seth Godin, Deep Work by Cal Newport, Steal Like an Artist by Austin Kleon, The 4-Hour Workweek, and The Power of Now. There are more.

stories.title: Music I return to
stories.text: I return to Rammstein, Metallica, Ólafur Arnalds, Lights & Motion, Krishna Das, Tara Brach, Lane 8, and Purple Disco Machine. My playlists have less strategic coherence than my product roadmap.

stories.title: Learning piano
stories.text: I'm trying to learn piano whenever I find one, including the occasional piano in a mall or park. I wouldn't call myself accomplished yet.
topics: what do you do for fun

stories.title: A hobby on my list
stories.text: I keep saying I'll start pottery so I can make strange coffee and tea mugs. It has been in my backlog long enough to qualify as an enterprise feature.

stories.title: Sports I follow
stories.text: I don't follow a sport or a team. I refuse to fake a lifelong allegiance for better small talk.

stories.title: Cats and dogs
stories.text: I like both cats and dogs. More animals make this world a happier place.

stories.title: A small thing that improves my day
stories.text: A walk without my phone makes my day better. It also means I can't check on my AI agents for a little while, which is probably healthy.

stories.title: Why I started building
stories.text: I like the moment an idea stops being a slide and does something for a real person. Building lets me use creativity and analytical thinking to bring a product or business idea to life.

stories.title: My first business
stories.text: In grad school, I started a crowdfunding platform for artisans from developing nations who had traditionally relied on microloans. It was an early lesson that building and getting discovered are different jobs.

stories.title: What I enjoy about work
stories.text: I enjoy taking a messy problem, making something people can use, and watching where they click instead of where I hoped they'd click. That last part keeps my ego honest.

stories.title: How I think about shipping
stories.text: Version one is a way to learn from reality before spending six months polishing the wrong thing. I still build it properly; I just don't confuse properly with never launching.

stories.title: How I think about discovery
stories.text: A good product does not automatically come with an audience. People need a way to find it, understand it, and trust it. Search, including AI search, needs clear answers and credible evidence; it does not owe anyone a ranking.
